 Judgment

This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:-
On 23.03.2022 at about 2.00 pm., when the petitioner was riding the Deo Scooter bearing reg.No.KA-11-EN-6327 on the extreme left side of Malavalli-Mysore Road slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached in front of TVS Show room, Malavalli Town, Mandya, at that time, suddenly the driver of Canter bearing reg No.KA-09-D-5068 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner.
As a result the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

Immediately, the petitioner was shifted to Malavalli Govt Hospital wherein he took first aid treatment and then referred to Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences and Teaching Hospital, Mandya wherein he took treatment as inpatient from 23.03.2022 to 30.03.2022 and spent more than Rs.80,000/- towards medicines, conveyance,
nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,

entities.text: Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences and Teaching Hospital, Mandya
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, brilliant student, studying 1 st year B.Com and use to participate in co-curricular activities.
It is further contended that the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-09- D-5068 by its driver.
The Malavalli Town Police have registered a criminal case against the driver of Canter in Cr.No.20/2022 U/Sec.279 & 338 of IPC.
After investigation Police have filed Charge Sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondent No.1 & 2 being the Owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore petitioner constrained to file a petition and sought for awarding compensation.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court hence, he has been placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 has appeared through his counsel and filed the objections to main petition.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its objection that the denying the petition averments.
Respondent has contended that, there is 2 days delay in lodging the complaint hence, denied the involvement of Canter vehicle in the alleged accident.

It is the contention of the respondent that, as per MLC extract of the Malavalli Government Hospital it has mentioned that, "fall from bike near TVS show room around 3.00 pm., details not known bike and bike" it is self accident and said hospital also issued wound certificate.

In Mandya Hospital also it is has mentioned in MLC as "History of alleged RTA on 23.03.2022 at 1.00 pm., near Malavalli Town, patient was riding the two wheeler and fell down of lost control the bike".
Respondent also contended that, there a non joinder of necessary parties as not made the necessary parties of the motor cycle bearing reg.No.KA-11-EN-6327 such as owner and insurer.

Respondent has denied the issuance of policy in favour of Canter and the liability if any, shall be strictly subject to the terms and conditions of the policy and the petitioner has to put strict proof of the same.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
The driver of the Canter was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.
4. On the basis of above pleadings, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether petitioner proves that on 23.03.2021 at about 2.00 pm., while he was riding his Deo Scooter bearing reg.No.KA-11-EN-6327 on extreme left side of Malavalli - Mysore Road, when reached in front of TVS Show room, Malavalli Town,
Mandya, at that time, the driver of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-09-D- 5068 came with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to impact the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries in the alleged RTA ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9.
The driver of Canter vehicle has examined as PW.2 and got marked Ex.P.10.
One eye witness has examined as PW.3.
On behalf of respondent No.2, its Deputy Manager has examined as RW.1 and got marked 4 documents as Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed their side evidence.
6. Heard the arguments of both side.

7. My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;

-:R E A S O N S:-
8. Issue No.1:-
In order to prove the actionable negligence, the petitioner has got examined himself as PW-1.
He has got marked 9 documents as Ex-P1 to Ex-P9.
He has reiterated the averments of the petition in his affidavit filed for his examination- in-chief.

9. It is relevant to note that the respondent No.2 has specifically contended that as per MLC extract of the Malavalli Government Hospital it has mentioned that, "fall from bike near TVS show room around 3.00 pm., details not known bike and bike" it is self accident and said hospital also issued wound certificate.

In Mandya Hospital also it is has mentioned in MLC as "History of alleged RTA on 23.03.2022 at 1.00 pm., near Malavalli Town, patient was riding the two wheeler and fell down of lost control the bike".
Moreover, complaint lodged after lapse of 2 days from the date of accident.

Therefore, the burden is on the petitioner to prove that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of Canter.
10.

PW.1 has deposed that, on 23.03.2022 at about 2.00 pm., he was riding the Deo Scooter bearing reg.No.KA-11-EN-6327 on the extreme left side of Malavalli - Mysore Road slowly and cautiously, by observing the traffic rules and regulations and when he reached in front of TVS Show room,
Malavalli Town, Mandya, at that time, suddenly the driver of Canter bearing reg No.KA-09-D-5068 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner without observing traffic rules and regulations and dashed against him.
As a result he fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.

11. PW.1 in support of his version, he has produced the certified copy of FIR, complaint, crime details form with spot mahazar, charge sheet, seizer mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate, MLC register and discharge summary which are marked at Ex.P.1 to 9.
12.
I have perused Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.9.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 23.03.2021 at about 2.00 p.m. and the FIR at Ex.P.1 in crime No.0020/2022 came to be registered on 25.03.2022 at around 12.45, at Malavalli Town Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.

Ex.P.2 - complaint was lodged by relative of petitioner on 25.03.2022 wherein he has mentioned that due unconscious stage of petitioner, he came to lodge the complaint, Ex.P.3 - spot panchanama reveals that at the time of accident, Canter bearing No.KA- 09-D-5068 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner and due to over take from right side of petitioner's scooter,
canter vehicle touched the handle of scooter and caused the accident.
Accident took place at Malavalli - Mysore main road, in front of TVS show room.

Further the records reveal that thereafter the police conducted investigation and filed charge-sheet at Ex.P.4 against the driver of the offending Canter vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-09-D-5068 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337,
338 of IPC with 187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.5 - seized mahazar reveals the number plate of Canter bearing reg.No.KA-09-D-5068.
Ex.P.6 - IMV report of vehicle No.KA-09-D-5068 says as no visible damages found at the time of Inspection.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has deposed that,    
   .

..8   Accident between Bike and Bike    .

14. Petitioner has also examined examined driver of the offending Canter vehicle as PW.2 and through him got marked Ex.P.10.

During his cross-examination he has deposed that,   
        .

As per Ex.P.10 - order sheet in CC No.1429/2022 it comes to know that, accused pleaded guilty voluntarily and he has been convicted with total fine amount of Rs.7,000/-.
15.
Petitioner has also examined one eye witness as PW.3.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to PW.3 to disbelieve their version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.

Moreover, it is settled law that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

16. On the other hand, the Deputy Manager of respondent No.2 company has examined as RW.1 and got marked Ex.R.1 - authorisation letter, Ex.R.2 - MLC register, Ex.R.3 - discharge summary and Ex.R.4 - insurance policy.
As discussed above that, Pw.2/driver of offending Canter vehicle he himself pleaded guilty and moreover charge sheet also filed on him which has not been challenged by driver nor respondent.
Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the offending Canter which belongs to the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the affirmative.
17. Issue No.2:
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the RTA.
As already discussed above the petitioner has proved that the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of offending Canter bearing reg.No.KA-09-D-5068.
As per Ex.P4/wound certificate the petitioner sustained one grievous injury and two simple injuries in nature.

sentences.text: Moreover, the petitioner has not examined the doctor and also not produced any disability certificate to show that he is having physical disability.

Therefore, in view of non production of disability certificate and non examining of doctor regarding disability, it cannot be considered as the petitioner is having physical disability due to the accidental injuries.

Except discharge summary, the petitioner has not produced any medical bills and on perusal of Ex.P9/discharge summary of Mandya Institute of Medical Sciences, which discloses that the petitioner took treatment as inpatient from 23.03.2022 to 30.03.2022.
PW.1 has deposed that, he was a 1st Year B.Com student and as stated above there is no physical disability caused to the petitioner due to the accidental injuries.
Therefore, there is no question of awarding compensation for loss of future earnings.
Therefore, by considering the injuries sustained and treatment taken by him, it is just and proper to award the Global Compensation.

Hence, I am of the opinion that petitioner is entitled for Global Compensation of Rs.50,000/-.
19.
Regarding Liability:
As discussed at issue No.1 regarding the negligence of driver of Canter.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

As the policy was in force therefore,
the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
20. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.50,000/- (Fifty Thousand Only) with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation, entire amount shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification and verification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw up award accordingly.
